column12: Judgement: this is a published list price, which the brief puts ahead of the CMS convention, but it belongs to the comparator and not to velzatinib. The book's drug_demand table has no Qinlock, Ayvakit, Gleevec or Sutent rows, and data.cms.gov was unreachable, so no CMS per-beneficiary price could be read. The case against: Qinlock is a fourth-line drug for a very small population, and a second-line drug, or later a first-line one, may launch below it. The generic comparators (sunitinib, imatinib) cost a small fraction of this. column11: Three sourced parts. (1) 5,234 of 31,019 staged cases (16.87%) were distant at diagnosis (Patel & Benipal, Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120, PMID 31037234, Table 1). (2) Estimated 15-year recurrence-free survival after surgery without adjuvant therapy was 59.9%, so 40.1% recur (Joensuu H et al., Lancet Oncol 2012;13:265-74, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(11)70299-6, PMID 22153892, 2,560 patients pooled). 0.1687 + 0.8313 x 0.401 = 0.5021 of each year's diagnoses reach advanced disease. (3) The label reach: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926; ASCO 2026 TPS11588) excludes GIST that is wild-type for both KIT and PDGFRA and GIST with an activating PDGFRA exon 18 mutation. In advanced GIST (MetaGIST) KIT mutations are found in 82.8% and PDGFRA in 2.1% (Emile JF et al., Med Oncol 2012;29(3):1765-72, doi:10.1007/s12032-011-0074-y, PMID 21953054). 0.5021 x 0.828 = 0.4157
column12: Judgement: assumes every KIT-mutant patient reaching advanced disease eventually fails imatinib and is fit for a second line, and that the label follows the trial's exclusions. The case for lower: adjuvant imatinib now delays or prevents some recurrences, some patients stay on first-line imatinib for years, and some die or decline before second line. The case for higher: the incidence rate is out of date and rising, and non-exon-18 PDGFRA mutants (a share of the 2.1%) are eligible but left out here

column11: Hsu JT et al., 'Imatinib dose escalation versus sunitinib as a second-line treatment against advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors: a nationwide population-based cohort study', Oncotarget 2017;8(41):71128-37, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.16795, PMID 29050348 (Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, July 2004 to December 2010): of 521 advanced GIST patients failing first-line imatinib 400 mg and treated with dose escalation or sunitinib, 125 escalated then switched to sunitinib and 150 switched directly, so 275 (52.8%) received sunitinib after imatinib; 150 (28.8%) took it directly
column12: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0 on sunitinib's post-imatinib capture, assuming a head-to-head PFS win in StrateGIST 3 takes sunitinib's place. The anchor is sunitinib at any point after imatinib, including after dose escalation, because velzatinib's trial population is 'after imatinib' and escalation is still imatinib. The case for lower: the denominator excludes patients who received neither option (best supportive care, death before second line), so it overstates capture of the model's pool; the setting is Taiwan, not the US. The case for higher: sunitinib was reimbursed in Taiwan only from February 2009, part way through the 2004-2010 enrolment window, so its share there is depressed; a PFS win could also displace dose escalation
